external_entities.name: Customer
external_entities.description: A person who browses and orders socks through the Sokify mobile app, and who is sent a fax confirmation carrying their name and address.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The only customer-facing channel; customers browse and order through it. There is no website. It talks to the web API over HTTP.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app; there is no website.
processes.notes: Tagged pii because the app is the only stated route by which a customer's details reach the web API — the source rules out a website. It is not tagged financial: the source never says where payment details are captured, only that the database holds the card they paid with.

processes.name: Web API
processes.description: Receives traffic from the mobile app over HTTP, keeps customers in the user database, hands placed orders over to SIMS, and also receives SQL statements from the catalogue spreadsheet's macros.
processes.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS, it's on the list.
processes.notes: The source states outright that nobody can say what the API does about authentication, so every flow into it holds authentication unknown rather than absent.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system, running since long before the app existed. On receiving an order it writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it and sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
processes.source_excerpt: the API hands the order over to SIMS, our stock and inventory system, which has been running since long before the app existed

processes.name: Fax gateway
processes.description: Receives dispatch notes from SIMS and faxes the customer a confirmation carrying their name and address. It dials the number stored against the order, and nobody checks the fax arrived at the right place.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
processes.notes: The source does not say whether the gateway is operated in-house or by a third party; it is zoned with Sokify's own systems on the strength of being described as part of what SIMS does with an order.

processes.name: Catalogue spreadsheet
processes.description: The spreadsheet in which Marketing keep the catalogue; its macros send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy. Described as a stopgap that is still in place. It lives on a marketing laptop in the office.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
processes.notes: Typed as a process rather than an external entity: it is the org's own tooling and the source describes it by what its macros execute, not by who operates it. It is the resting place of the catalogue and the code that pushes SQL, and is modelled once.

data_stores.name: User database
data_stores.description: Holds customers as kept by the web API: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.data_classification: Customer name, address, and the card they paid with

data_stores.name: Delivery address flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS into which SIMS writes the delivery address for an order. Only addresses go in that file, nothing else.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else

data_flows.name: Confirmation fax

data_flows.notes: The stated absence is destination verification, not authentication in general — the source says nobody checks the fax arrived at the right place, and says nothing else about how this leg is controlled.

trust_boundaries.description: The server-side estate: the web API, the user database, SIMS, the flat file kept alongside SIMS, and the fax gateway.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the API hands the order over to SIMS, our stock and inventory system

trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The web API is reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: The mobile app is the only customer channel and talks to the web API over HTTP from customers' own devices.

assumptions.assumption: The customer and the mobile app sit outside Sokify's own systems, in a customer-device zone.
assumptions.basis: The app is the channel through which customers browse and order, and it reaches the web API over HTTP; the source names no other placement for it.

assumptions.assumption: The marketing laptop and its spreadsheet sit in a separate office zone from the server-side systems.
assumptions.basis: "The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office", distinct from where the web API and SIMS are described as running.
